symbols.name: T
symbols.def: Supplied or population-recovered undirected no-collider forest with components \(T_1,\ldots,T_c\).

symbols.name: Hjr
symbols.def: \(H_{j,r}\) orients every edge of \(T_j\) away from \(r\).

symbols.name: P
symbols.def: Population law of the centered observed vector.

symbols.name: K
symbols.def: Maximum number of distinct innovation-variance labels.

symbols.name: S
symbols.role: Exact numerical label set selected by a root.

symbols.name: Hrho
symbols.role: DAG encoded by a root tuple.

symbols.name: Qloc
symbols.def: \(Q_j(D)=\bigcap_{(u,v):\,uv\in E(T_j),\,b_{v\mid u}\notin D}T_{v;uv}\), where \(T_{v;uv}\) is the side containing \(v\) after deleting \(uv\), and an empty intersection equals \(V(T_j)\).

symbols.name: Rloc
symbols.role: Roots whose full signature lies in a dictionary.

symbols.name: pi
symbols.def: Supplied order of the forest components.

symbols.name: ell
symbols.def: Cut after the first \(\ell\) components in order \(\pi\).

symbols.name: U
symbols.role: Labels possibly used by one component.

symbols.name: Uall
symbols.role: Universe used by the independent ambiguity block.

symbols.name: tnew
symbols.role: Scale of the independent ambiguity block.

symbols.name: Bcut
symbols.role: Live recurring labels at a cut.

symbols.name: eta
symbols.def: Improvement in the exponential base below two.

symbols.name: fK
symbols.def: Arbitrary dependence on the primary parameter in an FPT algorithm or conditional lower bound.

symbols.name: N
symbols.def: Binary encoding length of \((T,\Sigma,K,\pi)\), with \(\pi\) omitted for unordered problems.

symbols.name: bCand
symbols.def: Candidate slots \((\widetilde b_{v\mid u})\) for both directions of every edge \(uv\in E(T_j)\).

symbols.name: cedge
symbols.def: \(c_{uv}\in\mathbb Q\setminus\{0\}\) satisfies \(c_{uv}^{2}=\widetilde a_u\widetilde a_v(1-h_{uv})\) for each \(uv\in E(T_j)\).

symbols.name: M
symbols.space: \(\mathbb S_{++}^{V(T_j)}\) for component realization and \(\mathbb S_{++}^{p}\) for full-covariance projection
symbols.def: Generic covariance matrix, used as a component covariance in inverse realization and as a full covariance variable in confidence projection.

symbols.name: Bcoef
symbols.def: \(B_\rho(M)\) places the population regression coefficients of each vertex on its parents in \(H_\rho\) and zero elsewhere.
symbols.role: Coefficient recovery under a candidate orientation.

symbols.name: ThetaHat
symbols.def: \(\widehat\Theta_{K,n}\) contains \(\theta_\rho(M;x,y)\) for every \(M\in\mathcal C_n\) and root tuple \(\rho\) whose signatures, computed from \(M\) by \(\text{def:root-signature}\), use at most \(K\) values.

assumptions.condition: \(P\) is faithful to the undirected forest \(T\), equivalently to every collider-free rooting assembled from the directed components \(H_{j,r}\).

standard.name: Gaussian causal faithfulness restricted to a forest

definitions.name: Rational faithful Gaussian forest inputs
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak M_{p,K}^{\mathrm{forest}}=\{(T,\Sigma,P,K):P=\mathcal N_p(0,\Sigma),\ P\text{ is faithful to }T,\ \Sigma\in\mathbb S_{++}^{p}\cap\mathbb Q^{p\times p},\ K\in\{0,\ldots,p\}\}\).

definitions.name: Exact component-root signature
definitions.construction: For every \(j\in\{1,\ldots,c\}\) and \(r\in V(T_j)\), compute \(S_j(r)=\{\Sigma_{rr}\}\cup\{\Sigma_{vv}-\Sigma_{vu}^{2}/\Sigma_{uu}:u\to v\text{ in }H_{j,r}\}\) by exact rational arithmetic.

definitions.name: Feasibility, uniqueness, and two-witness problems
definitions.construction: \(\textsc{K-Fiber}\) asks whether \(\mathcal F_K(\Sigma)\ne\varnothing\); \(\textsc{Unique-K-Fiber}\) asks whether \(|\mathcal F_K(\Sigma)|=1\); \(\textsc{Two-K-Fiber}\) returns two distinct tuples in \(\mathcal F_K(\Sigma)\) or certifies that fewer than two exist.

definitions.name: Live-label right-congruence state
definitions.construction: At cut \(\ell\), a prefix with used dictionary \(D\) is represented by \((A_\ell,b_\ell)=(D\cap B_\ell,|D\setminus B_\ell|)\); after choosing signature \(S_{\pi(\ell+1)}(r)\), set \(W=A_\ell\cup S_{\pi(\ell+1)}(r)\), \(A_{\ell+1}=W\cap B_{\ell+1}\), and \(b_{\ell+1}=b_\ell+|W\setminus B_{\ell+1}|\), retaining at most two backpointers per state.

definitions.name: Root-locus and realization handle for the \(K\)-frontier
definitions.construction: Starting move: represent every candidate dictionary by the component loci \((R_j(D))_{j=1}^{c}\), seek bounded certificates for an empty locus using half-tree intersections and root labels, and in the converse direction compile selector and compatibility incidences through \((\widetilde a_v,h_{uv},c_{uv})\). A compiled gadget is admissible only after the piecewise matrix with diagonal \(M_{xx}=\widetilde a_x\) and off-diagonal path products passes the arbitrary-root SEM covariance derivation, both directed residual identities on every edge, positive definiteness, nonzero-edge faithfulness, rationality, polynomial bit-length control, and enumeration of every internal root and auxiliary label.

definitions.name: Supplied-order lower-bound handle
definitions.construction: Starting move: take the incidence-path decomposition in the Set Cover reduction of Lampis, assign one recurring residual value to each live boundary element, and order Gaussian components by the source bags. Before using any component as a Gaussian gadget, certify its piecewise covariance \(M_{xx}=\widetilde a_x\) and off-diagonal path products by an arbitrary-root SEM derivation, check both directed residuals on every edge, positive definiteness, nonzero-edge faithfulness, rationality, and polynomial bit length; then prove that private realization labels never cross a cut and every unsatisfied obligation forces a new selected label.

definitions.name: Covariance-region projection
definitions.construction: Form \(\mathcal C_n\), retain every pair \((M,\rho)\) with \(M\in\mathcal C_n\) whose exact root signatures computed from \(M\) by \(\text{def:root-signature}\) use at most \(K\) values, and project the retained pairs through \(\theta_\rho(M;x,y)\) to obtain \(\widehat\Theta_{K,n}\).

statements.statement: For every input in \(\mathfrak M_{p,K}^{\mathrm{forest}}\), mapping a root tuple \(\rho\) to the forest DAG \(H_\rho\) is a bijection between \(\mathcal F_K(\Sigma)\) and the DAGs in the Markov-equivalence class of \(T\) whose Gaussian regression innovations take at most \(K\) distinct variances.
statements.justification: This converts an observational causal-structure fiber into an exact minimum-union problem without assuming its equality partition.
statements.gap: WuDrton2023 fixes the partition and compares whole models; this theorem is pointwise in one covariance and existentially selects its canonical equality classes.
statements.consumer: SEMgraph can use the bijection to report every orientation compatible with at most \(K\) exact innovation levels.

statements.statement: Fix a component \(T_j\). Positive rational arrays \((\widetilde a_v,\widetilde b_{v\mid u})\) are the vertex variances and both directed-edge regression residuals of a rational positive-definite Gaussian covariance faithful to \(T_j\) if and only if, for every edge \(uv\), there is \(h_{uv}\in(0,1)\cap\mathbb Q\) with \(\widetilde b_{v\mid u}=\widetilde a_vh_{uv}\), \(\widetilde b_{u\mid v}=\widetilde a_uh_{uv}\), and \(\widetilde a_u\widetilde a_v(1-h_{uv})\) a nonzero square in \(\mathbb Q\). Choose a signed rational square root \(c_{uv}\ne0\) on every edge and define the matrix piecewise by \[M_{xx}=\widetilde a_x,\qquad M_{xy}=\frac{\prod_{uv\in\operatorname{path}(x,y)}c_{uv}}{\prod_{z\in\operatorname{intpath}(x,y)}\widetilde a_z}\quad(x\ne y).\] For every root \(r\in V(T_j)\), the linear SEM oriented away from \(r\), with edge coefficient \(c_{uv}/\widetilde a_u\) for \(u\to v\), root innovation variance \(\widetilde a_r\), and nonroot innovation variance \(\widetilde a_vh_{uv}>0\) for \(u\to v\), has covariance exactly \(M\). Consequently \(M\) is positive definite and faithful to \(T_j\), and on every edge \(uv\) it satisfies \(M_{vv}-M_{vu}^{2}/M_{uu}=\widetilde a_vh_{uv}=\widetilde b_{v\mid u}\) and \(M_{uu}-M_{uv}^{2}/M_{vv}=\widetilde a_uh_{uv}=\widetilde b_{u\mid v}\). Conversely, every rational positive-definite covariance faithful to \(T_j\) yields these conditions with \(c_{uv}=M_{uv}\), obeys the same piecewise tree-product formula, and has nonzero edge covariances. Each path entry uses at most \(|V(T_j)|-1\) rational products and divisions, so all entries have bit length polynomial in the slot representation. As a nonunit-diagonal check, for the path \(1-2-3\), take \((\widetilde a_1,\widetilde a_2,\widetilde a_3)=(3,7/4,23/16)\), \((c_{12},c_{23})=(3/2,7/8)\), and \((h_{12},h_{23})=(4/7,16/23)\). The formula gives \[M=\begin{pmatrix}3&3/2&3/4\\3/2&7/4&7/8\\3/4&7/8&23/16\end{pmatrix},\] whose leading principal minors are \(3,3,3\); its directed residuals are \((\widetilde b_{2\mid1},\widetilde b_{1\mid2})=(1,12/7)\) and \((\widetilde b_{3\mid2},\widetilde b_{2\mid3})=(1,28/23)\), and its nonzero edge covariances make the Gaussian path faithful.
statements.justification: The piecewise construction and arbitrary-root SEM identity isolate exactly which abstract label gadgets compile into faithful rational Gaussian tree signatures.
statements.gap: BoegeKubjasMisraSolus2026 gives rational parameter recovery and fixed-color model ideals but not inverse simultaneous realization across alternative roots or bit-complexity control.
statements.consumer: A hardness reduction for \(\textsc{K-Fiber}\) may invoke this certificate only after checking its edge residuals, positive definiteness, faithfulness, rationality, and bit length; algorithms can exploit the same forced identities.

statements.statement: For every component \(T_j\) and dictionary \(D\), \(R_j(D)=\{r\in V(T_j):S_j(r)\subseteq D\}\). Moreover, \(Q_j(D)\) is empty or a connected subtree, and \(R_j(D)\) is computable in time polynomial in \(N\).
statements.justification: The locus is the main symbolic invariant separating Gaussian root signatures from arbitrary multiple-choice label systems.
statements.gap: Neither fixed-partition CPDAG closure nor generic minimum-label complexity supplies a subtree-intersection description of roots supported by a numerical dictionary.
statements.consumer: The locus gives polynomial dictionary verification and the branching certificates used by exact fiber solvers.

statements.statement: Given \((T,\Sigma,K,\pi)\), the live-label state in \(\text{def:ordered-state}\) decides \(\textsc{K-Fiber}\), decides \(\textsc{Unique-K-Fiber}\), and solves \(\textsc{Two-K-Fiber}\) exactly with at most \((K+1)2^{q_\pi}\) states per cut and \((K+1)2^{q_\pi}\operatorname{poly}(N)\) bit operations.
statements.justification: It gives the exact positive side of the supplied-order frontier and handles decision and multiplicity with one right congruence.
statements.gap: Lampis2025 treats graph-decomposition interfaces; recurring exact residual values may retire and reappear and require the separate completed-label count.
statements.consumer: A component ordering with small label recurrence yields an implementable exact sensitivity analysis for bottom-up equal-variance discovery.

statements.statement: If \(d=\max_j|V(T_j)|\), all three problems in \(\text{def:k-fiber-problems}\) are solvable in \(d^K\operatorname{poly}(N,K)\) time by branching on the root signatures of a component with empty locus and deduplicating terminal root tuples.
statements.justification: This proves a nontrivial FPT boundary and rules out hardness gadgets built only from bounded-size components.
statements.gap: Generic minimum-label hardness allows unrestricted choice systems and does not respect the bounded root domain induced by a forest component.
statements.consumer: Sparse applications with uniformly small chain components obtain exact root and ambiguity recovery even if the unrestricted \(K\)-frontier is hard.

statements.statement: Using \(t>\max U_0\), append the independent covariance block \(\begin{psmallmatrix}4t&2t\\2t&4t\end{psmallmatrix}\). Its two roots have the identical signature \(\{4t,3t\}\), disjoint from \(U_0\). Thus the original \(\textsc{K-Fiber}\) instance is nonempty if and only if the augmented instance has two distinct witnesses at budget \(K+2\); appending the block last preserves \(q_\pi\).
statements.justification: This is a query-correct Gaussian transfer from decision to actual two-witness recovery rather than a raw dictionary analogy.
statements.gap: YatoSeta2003 requires solution-preserving reductions; the equal-signature faithful block supplies that missing property for this direction only.
statements.consumer: A lower bound or solver for feasibility immediately yields a certified consequence for two-witness ambiguity.

statements.statement: If \(\rho\in\mathcal F_1(\Sigma)\), then \(\mathcal F_1(\Sigma)=\{\rho\}\). Hence the latent-budget fiber reduces at \(K=1\) to the equal-error-variance uniqueness conclusion of PetersBuhlmann2014.
statements.justification: The reduction is the required endpoint check for the new fiber definition.
statements.gap: PetersBuhlmann2014 proves the general equal-variance identification result; this proposition verifies that the new combinatorial target has exactly that endpoint.
statements.consumer: Users selecting \(K=1\) recover the familiar unique-orientation interpretation rather than a different estimand.

statements.statement: Using the handle in \(\text{def:k-frontier-handle}\), determine whether \(\textsc{K-Fiber}\) on \(\mathfrak M_{p,K}^{\mathrm{forest}}\) has an \(f(K)\operatorname{poly}(N)\) decision-and-witness algorithm. If it does not, establish faithful rational W[1]- or W[2]-hardness with transformed budget linear in the source parameter and derive the corresponding ETH exclusion of \(f(K)N^{o(K)}\) time. Every negative-branch gadget must use the piecewise realization of \(\text{thm:rational-tree-realization}\) and independently verify the arbitrary-root SEM covariance identity, both directed residuals on each edge, positive definiteness, nonzero-edge faithfulness, rationality, polynomial bit length, every internal root, and every auxiliary label. The resolution must remain valid on the twin-star family.
statements.justification: This is the answer-open theorem-level kernel: it classifies whether latent equality information can be exploited without enumerating \(N^{K}\) dictionaries.
statements.gap: WuDrton2023 and PetersBuhlmann2014 settle supplied partitions and \(K=1\), while FellowsGuoKanj2010 settles unrestricted label systems; neither determines the Gaussian-realizable latent-\(K\) frontier.
statements.consumer: The classification tells SEMgraph whether an exact latent-\(K\) bottom-up mode can scale with the number of variance groups or must expose a hardness warning.

statements.statement: Construct a parameter-preserving classification of \(\textsc{Unique-K-Fiber}\): either give an algorithm matching the resolved feasibility frontier or build a canonical isolation or solution-preserving reduction that decides whether exactly one root tuple belongs to \(\mathcal F_K(\Sigma)\), without treating numerical label renamings as distinct witnesses and without increasing \(q_\pi\) by more than a constant.
statements.justification: Uniqueness is the actual structural-identification decision and is not implied by a nonemptiness classification.
statements.gap: Generic Another Solution theory warns that decision and uniqueness can differ; no published Gaussian variance-fiber reduction preserves the canonical root-tuple solution set.
statements.consumer: The result distinguishes a uniquely oriented latent-\(K\) SEM from one with genuine structural ambiguity.

statements.statement: Using \(\text{def:q-lower-handle}\), prove that for every \(\eta>0\) no algorithm solves the supplied-order \(\textsc{K-Fiber}\) problem in \((2-\eta)^{q_\pi}\operatorname{poly}(N,K)\) time under the primal-pathwidth SETH, on rational covariances faithful to no-collider forests, or exhibit a strictly smaller sufficient state that refutes the proposed base-two frontier. A lower-bound construction may invoke \(\text{thm:rational-tree-realization}\) only after its piecewise diagonal and off-diagonal formula has been certified through the arbitrary-root SEM covariance identity, both directed residuals on every edge, positive definiteness, nonzero-edge faithfulness, rationality, polynomial bit length, and exact preservation of the crossing-label set.
statements.justification: This exposes the true open content behind the natural subset-state algorithm rather than presenting its upper bound as optimal by analogy.
statements.gap: Lampis2025 proves base-two barriers for Set Cover incidence pathwidth, not for numerical residual labels whose Gaussian realization may create extra crossing values.
statements.consumer: The lower bound certifies when reordering components, rather than improving the state base, is the only route to faster exact analysis.

statements.statement: Under \(X^{(1)},\ldots,X^{(n)}\stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}\mathcal N_p(0,\Sigma)\) and \(c_\alpha^2\ge p(p+1)/(n\alpha)\), the construction in \(\text{def:projection}\) satisfies \(\mathbb P_\Sigma\{\Theta_K(\Sigma;x,y)\subseteq\widehat\Theta_{K,n}\}\ge1-\alpha\). The same event simultaneously retains every orientation in \(\mathcal F_K(\Sigma)\).
statements.justification: The proposition supplies honest structure-aware uncertainty without applying exact equality directly to the sample covariance.
statements.gap: StriederDrton2023 treats the all-equal model and WangKolarDrton2026 projects ordering confidence sets; neither projects through an unknown at-most-\(K\) equality fiber.
statements.consumer: SEMgraph can return a conservative orientation and total-effect sensitivity set rather than a selected-graph interval.

sampling_model.design: Observational covariance-fiber analysis with no interventions; the population complexity problem receives exact rational \(\Sigma\).
sampling_model.units: For the inference rung, \(X^{(1)},\ldots,X^{(n)}\) are independent centered Gaussian vectors in \(\mathbb R^p\).
sampling_model.treatment: No designated treatment is needed for orientation recovery; optional vertices \(x\) and \(y\) index a total-effect projection.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The population kernel uses exact Schur complements. The inference rung uses a simultaneous covariance region and performs no direct equality test on \(\widehat\Sigma\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The directed acyclic graph can be recovered from the joint Gaussian distribution under equal error variances.
Sources are identified by the smallest marginal variance, followed by conditional-variance source removal.
The variables are partitioned into blocks and each block shares the same error variance.
A generic distribution in a vertex-colored Gaussian DAG model is faithful to its DAG.
The minimum-label problems considered are W[2]-hard in the number of used labels.
Binary CSP on graph classes of unbounded treewidth has an ETH lower bound with a treewidth-over-log-treewidth exponent.
Set Cover has a base-two incidence-pathwidth barrier under the primal-pathwidth SETH.
An ASP reduction induces a polynomial-time bijection between the solution sets of the two instances.
An FPT-computable neighborhood function yields ordered Delay-FPT enumeration through a priority queue.
Split likelihood-ratio inversion gives finite-sample-valid total-effect confidence regions under equal variances.
Residual goodness-of-fit tests are inverted to construct confidence sets for causal orderings.

tldr: Arbitrary Gaussian error variances identify only a Markov-equivalence class, one common variance identifies the DAG, and a supplied partial-homoscedastic partition refines the class. This project studies the missing observational regime in which the equality partition is not supplied: a faithful rational Gaussian forest covariance is compatible with a root tuple when its exact regression residuals use at most \(K\) numerical values. The paper derives the root-signature structure and a piecewise rational tree realization whose diagonal is fixed separately from its off-diagonal path products; an arbitrary-root SEM identity certifies the covariance, both directed edge residuals, positive definiteness, faithfulness, rationality, and polynomial bit length. It settles the exact supplied-order dynamic program and makes the central theorem an honest FPT-versus-parameterized-hard classification in \(K\), with separate obligations for uniqueness, two-witness recovery, and the matching recurrence-width lower bound. A covariance-region projection then propagates sampling uncertainty to orientations and total effects.

project_justification.gap: Published equal-variance and partial-homoscedastic theory either fixes one common level or supplies the equality partition. Generic minimum-label hardness does not survive the algebraic and arithmetic restrictions of Gaussian residual signatures.
project_justification.niche: The exact latent-\(K\) covariance fiber is a pointwise structural-identification object lying between fully identified equal-error models and unrestricted Markov equivalence, with a parameter whose algorithmic status is unknown.
project_justification.fill: The project gives a root-union reduction, an exact rational tree-signature realization theorem with the piecewise diagonal and path-product covariance reconstructed by an arbitrary-root SEM, symbolic root loci, positive algorithms at bounded component size and bounded recurrence width, and an answer-open classification theorem whose negative branch must certify edge residuals, positive definiteness, faithfulness, rationality, and bit length before using any Gaussian gadget.

related_work: Peters and Buehlmann (2014) establish full identification when all innovation variances are equal, the \(K=1\) endpoint. Chen, Drton, and Wang (2019) exploit the same common-variance ordering to build scalable recovery algorithms. Wu and Drton (2023) characterize Gaussian DAG equivalence when the variance partition is supplied and therefore motivate the latent-partition step without occupying it. Boege, Kubjas, Misra, and Solus (2026) provide rational parameter recovery, algebraic Markov descriptions, and generic faithfulness for fixed vertex colorings; the inverse theorem here instead couples every alternative root of one covariance and certifies its piecewise diagonal and off-diagonal tree-product matrix by an arbitrary-root SEM calculation, including both directed edge residuals and polynomial bit length. Fellows, Guo, and Kanj (2010) show that several unrestricted minimum-label graph problems are W[2]-hard, but their label systems are not Gaussian-realizable. Marx (2010) and Lampis (2025) supply decomposition and fine-grained lower-bound techniques for CSP and Set Cover interfaces. Yato and Seta (2003) and Creignou et al. (2013) show why another-solution recovery needs solution-preserving reductions and a canonical neighborhood. Strieder and Drton (2023) and Wang, Kolar, and Drton (2026) motivate projecting structural uncertainty to total effects; the projection proposition here is deliberately supporting rather than advertised as a new optimal inference theorem.
technical_internal_limitation: A common-center star encoding of Set Cover has a universal two-label center-root witness, while varying centers creates complementary residual labels. Moreover, every edge satisfies \(a_u b_{v\mid u}=a_v b_{u\mid v}\), and rational covariance requires a rational-square edge reconstruction. The first reduction test therefore enumerates one three-choice selector and one compatibility component, including all internal roots; any unintended witness or nonconstant auxiliary-label charge rejects that template. The existing twin-star family also rules out raw representative compression at empty width-one cuts, but it does not rule out a different symbolic FPT algorithm.
honest_scope: The root-union, root-locus, bounded-choice, ordered-state, piecewise rational-realization, two-witness-transfer, and projection claims are statements to prove, supported only by presolve derivations and finite checks. The realization claim includes an exact three-vertex nonunit-diagonal check, but its general sufficiency still requires the arbitrary-root SEM covariance identity and its general necessity still requires the tree-product, faithfulness, rationality, and polynomial-bit-length arguments. No hardness or lower-bound construction may treat that certificate as available without verifying those obligations for every gadget. The headline \(K\)-classification, the arbitrary-algorithm \(q_\pi\) lower bound, and the uniqueness transfer remain open-ended questions. The proposition at \(K=1\) is the required reduction to PetersBuhlmann2014. The confidence projection claims coverage but not efficient optimization, likelihood-ratio calibration, unknown-mean adjustment, or robustness to approximate equality.

seed_details.anchor: WuDrton2023, Theorems 3.1, 3.4, and 4.1 and Section 6; FellowsGuoKanj2010, abstract and reduction sections.
seed_details.opportunity: Classify feasibility of an observationally induced, unknown error-variance partition with at most \(K\) blocks on a faithful Gaussian forest.
seed_details.theorem_kernel: Give an exact FPT-versus-parameterized-hard classification of \(\textsc{K-Fiber}\). The positive branch must construct an \(f(K)\operatorname{poly}(N)\) root-recovery map; the negative branch must give a faithful rational Gaussian reduction with parameter \(K'=O(k)\) and the corresponding \(f(K)N^{o(K)}\) ETH exclusion.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Wu and Drton begin with a supplied partition, while Fellows, Guo, and Kanj begin with arbitrary label incidences. The first new step is either a symbolic compression of exact Schur-residual dictionaries or a Gaussian selector-and-compatibility realization that excludes every unintended root.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for unknown partial-homoscedastic partitions, \(K\) distinct Gaussian DAG error variances, and Gaussian forest minimum-label parameterization returned fixed-partition or all-equal results but no latent-budget classification.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from generic minimum-label hardness because a root merely selects a label set.
seed_details.rebuttal: Gaussian signatures obey shared-edge product identities, rational-square constraints, and compulsory internal-root alternatives, so an abstract label reduction does not preserve the promised input class or the decision query.

seed_details.anchor: BoegeKubjasMisraSolus2026, Lemma 4, Theorems 6 and 9, Propositions 13 and 14, and Questions 16 and 21.
seed_details.opportunity: Characterize the exact collision and separation patterns simultaneously induced across all rootings of one rational Gaussian forest covariance.
seed_details.theorem_kernel: Derive a necessary-and-sufficient root-signature realization criterion using vertex variances, edge attenuations, and rational-square conditions. Define \(M_{xx}=\widetilde a_x\) and, only for \(x\ne y\), define \(M_{xy}\) by the edge-product over the path divided by its internal vertex variances; then prove with an arbitrary-root SEM that this is exactly the covariance, gives both directed residuals on every edge, is positive definite and faithful, remains rational, and has polynomial bit length.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Boege et al. push a fixed coloring through one rational DAG parametrization. The inverse problem fixes an arbitrary root, assigns coefficient \(c_{uv}/\widetilde a_u\) to each edge \(u\to v\), root innovation variance \(\widetilde a_r\), and nonroot innovation variance \(\widetilde a_vh_{uv}\), and must show that the resulting covariance equals the piecewise matrix for every alternative root.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for colored Gaussian inverse realization, forest root-residual signatures, and rational faithful signature patterns found fixed-color model geometry but no cross-root incidence theorem.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from saturation of the colored conditional-independence ideal.
seed_details.rebuttal: Saturation characterizes one fixed colored model over the reals; it does not impose simultaneous alternative-root equalities, exact separations, rational points, or bounded bit length.

seed_details.anchor: GuoPerkovic2021, Theorems on minimal effect enumeration; WuDrton2023, fixed-partition equivalence characterization.
seed_details.opportunity: Collapse structural root multiplicity to the distinct total-effect functionals carried by a latent-\(K\) forest fiber.
seed_details.theorem_kernel: For treatment and outcome in one tree, prove that the total-effect set is contained in \(\{0,\beta_{x\rightsquigarrow y}(\Sigma)\}\), characterize presence of each value by two constrained root-locus feasibility predicates, and recover effect-distinct witnesses with the supplied-order dynamic program.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Guo and Perkovic split an MPDAG by orienting a shortest problematic edge. Here unique-path geometry supplies two local effect classes, but membership of either class is decided by the globally coupled variance-label budget.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for latent variance-budget effect enumeration and Gaussian root-tuple effect duplicates found fixed-partition effect identification but no latent-budget functional fiber.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate because a directed tree path either points from treatment to outcome or it does not.
seed_details.rebuttal: The two numerical values are local, but whether either class intersects the global at-most-\(K\) fiber and how to recover a witness at the stated width are not local orientation questions.

seed_details.anchor: Lampis2025, Theorem 1.1 and Section 5.3; Marx2010, decomposition algorithm and ETH lower-bound framework.
seed_details.opportunity: Determine the exact base of the subset-state dynamic program under a supplied component order.
seed_details.theorem_kernel: Prove correctness of the \((K+1)2^{q_\pi}\operatorname{poly}(N)\) right-congruence dynamic program and exclude \((2-\eta)^{q_\pi}\operatorname{poly}(N)\) time under primal-pathwidth SETH by a \(q_\pi\)-preserving faithful rational reduction.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Lampis transfers one bit per incidence-path boundary element. The first changed step is realizing each live obligation as an exact recurring Gaussian residual label without adding crossing auxiliary labels or cheap roots.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for recurring numerical-label cut width and Gaussian forest subset-state lower bounds found no use of \(q_\pi\) in causal discovery.
seed_details.red_team: A standard pathwidth dynamic program and standard base-two lower bound.
seed_details.rebuttal: The upper-state congruence is specific to labels that may disappear and recur, and the lower bound requires a new numerical Gaussian realization preserving the supplied order and its exact crossing set.

seed_details.anchor: YatoSeta2003, Definition 2.5 and Proposition 2.1; CreignouKtariMeierMullerOliveVollmer2013, neighborhood-function theorem.
seed_details.opportunity: Classify uniqueness and another-witness recovery when numerical signature coincidences make label-renamed representations spurious.
seed_details.theorem_kernel: Canonicalize solutions as component-root tuples, establish query-correct reductions among feasibility, uniqueness, and second-witness recovery, and preserve \(K\) and \(q_\pi\) up to certified constants.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The Another Solution framework requires a solution-preserving map. A nonemptiness-preserving covariance gadget is insufficient until its two root extensions and all numerical-label symmetries are enumerated exactly.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for equal-error Gaussian DAG second solutions and root-fiber uniqueness found only generic another-solution and enumeration theory.
seed_details.red_team: One decision-oracle call can simply exclude the supplied tuple.
seed_details.rebuttal: Excluding one tuple is a disjunction outside the base input language; prefix restrictions or a faithful solution-bijective gadget must be implemented without increasing the parameters.

seed_details.anchor: StriederDrton2023, Theorems 1 and 2 and Section 5; WangKolarDrton2026, ordering-set coverage theorem.
seed_details.opportunity: Propagate covariance uncertainty through an existential union over root tuples and variance partitions.
seed_details.theorem_kernel: Project a simultaneous Gaussian covariance region through the latent-\(K\) forest fiber to orientations and total effects, prove joint coverage, and seek an executable projection with regular-stratum shrinking and singular-collision fallback.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The all-equal union has one residual level. The latent-\(K\) union requires simultaneous treatment of unknown equality partitions that merge at nonregular intersections.
seed_details.destination_search: The fixed-pair partial-homoscedastic inference problem is occupied by Strieder and Drton (2025); no source was found for projection through an unknown at-most-\(K\) partition.
seed_details.red_team: Coverage follows tautologically by projecting any valid confidence region.
seed_details.rebuttal: Raw coverage is only a supporting proposition; the publishable statistical kernel would require computable projection and shrinking across regular and singular strata.

seed_details.anchor: GaoTaiAragam2022, Theorems 2.1 and 3.1; StriederDrton2023, sensitivity discussion.
seed_details.opportunity: Replace exact equality by a scale-aware tolerance and identify the first tolerance at which orientation or effect ambiguity enters.
seed_details.theorem_kernel: Define \(\delta^*(\Sigma,K)\) as the smallest residual-variance tolerance for which two effect-distinct root tuples admit a \(K\)-center cover, and characterize it as a finite bottleneck over root signatures with a uniform plug-in guarantee.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Gao, Tai, and Aragam compare conditional variances to a fixed recovery gap. The new first step is optimizing the gap jointly over root choices, label centers, and effect equivalence rather than assuming one common population variance.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches found variance-gap recovery at \(K=1\) and simulation sensitivity, but no critical tolerance for a latent equality budget.
seed_details.red_team: A finite clustering problem on already computed residuals.
seed_details.rebuttal: The nontrivial object is the first effect-identification breakdown over a globally coupled root fiber, but without a sharper inferential theorem this remains below the selected complexity kernel.

seed_details.anchor: CreignouKtariMeierMullerOliveVollmer2013, ordered Delay-FPT theorem; GuoPerkovic2021, minimal effect enumeration theorem.
seed_details.opportunity: Enumerate each numerical or effect-distinct latent-\(K\) witness exactly once with parameterized delay.
seed_details.theorem_kernel: Construct a neighborhood function on canonical root tuples using constrained suffix feasibility and prove duplicate-free Delay-FPT enumeration under bounded recurrence width.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Creignou et al. exploit monotone graph modifications. Root tuples have no inclusion order, so the first changed step is a prefix neighborhood whose feasibility is certified by the live-label right congruence.
seed_details.destination_search: No ordered enumeration result for Gaussian variance fibers was found; adjacent causal work removes effect duplicates but does not impose a latent label budget.
seed_details.red_team: Routine backtracking after the decision dynamic program.
seed_details.rebuttal: Polynomial delay and exact-once output require a proved canonical neighborhood and duplicate control; nevertheless this is best treated as a follow-on result.

literature_map.anchor_read: BoegeKubjasMisraSolus2026 was read at the Introduction, Lemma 4, Theorems 6, 9, and 11, Propositions 13--14, Example 4, Questions 16 and 21, and Discussion.
adjacent_threads: WuDrton2023 supplies the exact Schur-complement equations for fixed within-block variance equality.
PetersBuhlmann2014 supplies the conditional-variance orientation mechanism at one color.

The Gaussian-tree product parametrization supplies only the off-diagonal destination construction: \(M_{xx}=\widetilde a_x\) is fixed separately, while for \(x\ne y\) the covariance is the product of edge covariances divided by internal vertex variances; the arbitrary-root SEM calculation must certify this entire piecewise matrix.
Generic minimum-label hardness exposes the incidence patterns a rational realization theorem would need to compile.
literature_map.occupancy_result: Fixed vertex-colored models are generically faithful, but no source characterizes exact equality and separation incidences across all rootings of one covariance or gives rational bit bounds.
exemplars_used: BoegeKubjasMisraSolus2026 as writing and algebraic-method exemplar
